prompt: Give the child 3 picture cards, mixed up: eating, putting the plate away, taking a plate. Say: 'Put the cards in a line, the way it happens.' Then ask: 'What do you do first? What do you do last?' Expected: taking a plate, then eating, then putting the plate away.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if all 3 cards are in the right order, else 0. Watch: does the child start with the plate, and use first/last words? Strategy: names the steps aloud, acts them out, copies a neighbour, guesses. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects).

prompt: Give the child 4 picture cards, mixed up: eating, washing hands, putting the plate away, taking a plate. Say: 'Put the cards in a line, the way it happens.' Then ask: 'What do you do first? What next? What then? What last?' Expected: washing hands, then taking a plate, then eating, then putting the plate away.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if all 4 cards are in order. Watch: first/next/then/last, and whether washing hands is placed before the plate. Strategy: acts it out, names each step, guesses. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects).

prompt: Give the child 4 picture cards, mixed up: big plant, seed, tree, small plant. Say: 'Put the cards in a line, the way it happens.' Then ask: 'Which one is first? Which one is last?' Expected: seed, then small plant, then big plant, then tree.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if all 4 cards are in order. Plants may be shown from a picture book or drawn by the teacher. Watch: seed is first, tree is last. Strategy: points while naming, compares sizes, guesses. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects).

prompt: No cards. Ask: 'What do you do first after waking up? What do you do next? And then?' Let the child answer in words or by showing with actions. Expected: at least 3 steps from the child's own morning, in an order that can really happen (a step is not missing or backwards).
teacherNote: Mark 1 if 3 steps are given in a believable order, else 0. Accept any real routine. Watch for first/next/then words. Strategy: acts steps out, recalls a story of the morning, lists without order. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects).

prompt: No cards. Ask: 'Show me with your hands and tell me how you put on socks and shoes. What do you do first? Next? Last?' Expected: socks on first, then shoes, then fasten or tie them; the child may show by acting.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if socks come before shoes and fastening comes last. This is the extension: the child gives the order without cards. Strategy: acts it out, names steps, guesses. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects).

prompt: Give the child a paper square and a paper triangle. Say: "Make a house with these two shapes." Do not show a picture of the house. Watch: does the child put the triangle on top? Does the child move or turn a piece to make it fit? Ask: "Which shapes did you use?"
teacherNote: Record Independent, Prompted or Supported apart from any mark. Strategy: tries pieces by trial, plans first, copies you. No picture is shown, so this tests building, not matching.

prompt: Give the child a paper circle and a paper triangle with its point up. Say: "Make an ice-cream cone with these two shapes." Watch: does the child turn the triangle so its point is down and put the circle on top? Ask: "How did you make it?"
teacherNote: This checks turning and repositioning a piece. Record Independent, Prompted (after a hint to turn it) or Supported (after you show a turn), apart from any mark.

prompt: This clown is made of shapes. Which shapes make it? Circle the answer.

prompt: In a relaxed one-to-one moment, ask: 'Count for me from 1 up to 20.' Do not use objects. Watch: is the right order kept, are any numbers skipped, is the step from single to double numbers hard (after 9, and the teens 13 to 19), does the child fix a mistake alone. Then ask: 'What comes after 14?' Expected: 1 to 20 in the right order with no number skipped; after 14 comes 15.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if all of 1 to 20 are in order. Write the last number reached, any number skipped, where the child hesitated, and whether the child corrected alone. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: sings a rhythm, uses fingers, restarts from 1 after a slip, stops at a number.

prompt: Give the child 4 blocks, put in a row on the table. Count from the left end, then from the right end. Watch: is the answer the same each time? Expected: 4 each time; the child says that the order or starting object does not change how many.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the child gets the same total both times and says (or shows) it did not change. Tell a counting slip (skips or counts one twice, total differs) from a concept slip (counts well but thinks the total will change). Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: points to each, touches and moves aside, uses fingers, guesses.

prompt: Give the child 5 buttons, put in a row on the table. Count from the left end, then start from the middle button and go on around. Watch: is the answer the same each time? Expected: 5 each time; the child says that the order or starting object does not change how many.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if both totals match and the child needs no recount. Tell a counting slip (skips or counts one twice, total differs) from a concept slip (counts well but thinks the total will change). Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: points to each, touches and moves aside, uses fingers, guesses.

prompt: Give the child 6 pebbles, put in a circle on the table. Count from any pebble the child picks, then from a different pebble. Watch: is the answer the same each time? Expected: 6 each time; the child says that the order or starting object does not change how many.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the totals match. Tell a counting slip (skips or counts one twice, total differs) from a concept slip (counts well but thinks the total will change). Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: points to each, touches and moves aside, uses fingers, guesses.

prompt: Give the child 8 bottle caps, put in a row on the table. Count from one end. Before the next count, ask: 'If we start from the other end, will we get the same number?' Let the child say, then count. Watch: is the answer the same each time? Expected: 8 each time; the child says that the order or starting object does not change how many.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the child predicts 'the same' and the counts agree. Say what the child predicted. Tell a counting slip (skips or counts one twice, total differs) from a concept slip (counts well but thinks the total will change). Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: points to each, touches and moves aside, uses fingers, guesses.

prompt: Give the child 10 ice-cream sticks, put in a heap on the table. Ask first: 'If you start with a different stick, will the answer change?' Then the child counts from two different starting sticks. Watch: is the answer the same each time? Expected: 10 each time; the child says that the order or starting object does not change how many.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the child predicts 'no change' and both counts match. Ask 'why?' and write the words. Tell a counting slip (skips or counts one twice, total differs) from a concept slip (counts well but thinks the total will change). Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: points to each, touches and moves aside, uses fingers, guesses.

Record fine-motor control separately (pencil grip, steadiness, whether lines meet), apart from the mark. A different context: a door. Watch that two sides are longer than the other two.

prompt: Draw a house in the box. Use a square for the wall and a triangle for the roof.
answer: The child draws a square with a triangle on top (two shapes, a house). Judge whether it can be recognised, not whether it is exact.
svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 440 240" width="440" height="240" role="img"><rect class="space" x="5" y="5" width="430" height="230" rx="10" fill="#fff" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/></svg>
teacherNote: Score the SHAPE only: 1 if it can be recognised as the shape, 0 if not; do not mark down a wobbly line. Record fine-motor control separately (pencil grip, steadiness, whether lines meet), apart from the mark. Extension: two shapes joined. A child who misses it but did the others does not necessarily lack the concept; shape understanding and drawing control are two things.

prompt: Show the classroom calendar. Ask: 'What day is today? What day was yesterday?' Part A, sequence: does the child say the day names correctly? Part B, understanding: does the child link yesterday to the day before today? Expected: today's day, and the day just before it.
teacherNote: Record two things apart: SEQUENCE (are the names in the right order, any skipped) and UNDERSTANDING (can the child use them: which day, how many, what comes next). Say whether the classroom calendar was used. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: sings it as a song, counts on fingers, looks at the calendar, guesses.

prompt: Part A, sequence: ask the child to say the days of the week in order, starting with Monday. Part B, understanding: ask 'How many days are in a week?' and 'What day comes after Sunday?' Expected: 7 days, in order; after Sunday comes Monday.
teacherNote: Record two things apart: SEQUENCE (are the names in the right order, any skipped) and UNDERSTANDING (can the child use them: which day, how many, what comes next). Say whether the classroom calendar was used. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: sings it as a song, counts on fingers, looks at the calendar, guesses.

prompt: Part A, sequence: ask 'What day comes after Wednesday?' Part B, understanding: ask 'What day comes before Friday?' and 'How did you know?' Expected: Thursday after Wednesday; Thursday before Friday; the child gives a reason, such as saying the days over.
teacherNote: Record two things apart: SEQUENCE (are the names in the right order, any skipped) and UNDERSTANDING (can the child use them: which day, how many, what comes next). Say whether the classroom calendar was used. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: sings it as a song, counts on fingers, looks at the calendar, guesses.

prompt: Part A, sequence: ask the child to say the months of the year in order, starting with January. Part B, understanding: ask 'Which month is it now?' and show it on the calendar. Expected: the 12 months in order; the child finds the present month.
teacherNote: Record two things apart: SEQUENCE (are the names in the right order, any skipped) and UNDERSTANDING (can the child use them: which day, how many, what comes next). Say whether the classroom calendar was used. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: sings it as a song, counts on fingers, looks at the calendar, guesses.

prompt: Part A, sequence: ask 'Which month comes after April?' Part B, understanding: ask the child to find that month on the calendar and say what comes after it. Expected: May after April, and June after May.
teacherNote: Record two things apart: SEQUENCE (are the names in the right order, any skipped) and UNDERSTANDING (can the child use them: which day, how many, what comes next). Say whether the classroom calendar was used. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: sings it as a song, counts on fingers, looks at the calendar, guesses.

prompt: Say the riddle aloud: 'I come just after 2. What number am I?' Offer counters or a number line only if the child needs them. Ask: 'How did you find it?' Expected: 3.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the number is right. Write the child's reasoning. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: counts on, uses the number line, uses counters or fingers, guesses. Within 10 first; teens last.

prompt: Say the riddle aloud: 'I come just before 6. What number am I?' Offer counters or a number line only if the child needs them. Ask: 'How did you find it?' Expected: 5.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the number is right. Write the child's reasoning. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: counts on, uses the number line, uses counters or fingers, guesses. Within 10 first; teens last.

prompt: Say the riddle aloud: 'I come between 7 and 9. What number am I?' Offer counters or a number line only if the child needs them. Ask: 'How did you find it?' Expected: 8.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the number is right. Write the child's reasoning. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: counts on, uses the number line, uses counters or fingers, guesses. Within 10 first; teens last.

prompt: Say the riddle aloud: 'I am more than 7. I am less than 10. I am not 8. What number am I?' Offer counters or a number line only if the child needs them. Ask: 'How did you find it?' Expected: 9.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the number is right. Write the child's reasoning. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: counts on, uses the number line, uses counters or fingers, guesses. Within 10 first; teens last.

prompt: Say the riddle aloud: 'I come between 12 and 14. What number am I?' Offer counters or a number line only if the child needs them. Ask: 'How did you find it?' Expected: 13. Teen number: use only after the child did well within 10.
teacherNote: Mark 1 if the number is right. Write the child's reasoning. Record help apart from the mark: Independent (alone), Prompted (after a spoken hint), Supported (needed demonstration or objects). Strategy: counts on, uses the number line, uses counters or fingers, guesses. Within 10 first; teens last.

prompt: One of these numerals means none. Circle it.
teacherNote: This question only checks that the child recognises 0. Writing 0 is checked separately in question 4. Ask "How do you know?" and write down the child's own words. Record Independent, Prompted or Supported apart from the mark.

prompt: Give the child 5 counters or stones and an empty cup. Say: "Put them all in the cup." Then show the empty table and ask: "How many are on the table now?" Then ask: "How do you know?" Last, if the child can write, ask the child to write the numeral for that number.
teacherNote: Accept "none", "nothing", "nothing is left" or "zero". Record three things separately: what the child says, the reasoning in the child's own words, and the writing of 0 (formation and direction). A child who cannot write yet may point to a numeral card. Record Independent, Prompted or Supported apart from the mark.

prompt: Hands-on. Give the child a small box and a counter. Say one at a time: "Put the counter IN the box." "Now ON the box." "Now UNDER the box" (lift it). "Now BESIDE the box." Then, if the child is ready: "IN FRONT OF the box." "BEHIND the box." Watch each placement.
teacherNote: Practical application. Record each word as Independent, Prompted or Supported (needs a demonstration). In, on, under and beside are expected; in front of and behind are an extension, so do not count them as a failure. Record separately from the receptive and expressive items.
